name: wardens
summary: Every turn you move two pieces: one warden and one raider, in either order.
Raiders only go forward, one square straight or diagonally. They capture by jumping exactly two squares in any of the eight directions, over anything in between.
Wardens step one square in any direction and never capture. An enemy raider standing next to one of your wardens is frozen: it can neither move nor capture.
Raiders capture wardens as well as raiders.
Get a raider to the far row to win.
If you cannot make both moves of your turn (every raider frozen or blocked, no raider left, or no warden left), you lose.
description: A game about two kinds of piece that can only work together, because every turn moves one of each. Raiders are the attack: they march forward and never step back (only a capture can carry one backward), and they strike only at a distance, jumping exactly two squares onto an enemy, so two raiders two squares apart are a standoff that whoever moves first wins. Wardens are the control: they cannot take anything, but any enemy raider next to a warden is frozen in place, unable to run or to strike. A warden walked up beside an enemy raider pins it for your raiders to take next turn, and a warden standing in front of your own line stops the raiders that would hit it; but a warden is itself a target for any raider two squares away, and losing all of them loses the game. Because raiders cannot retreat and a raider must move every turn, the board only ever tightens: the opening is a slow advance with wardens walked out as escorts, the middle game is a run of exchanges decided by who still has a safe raider move, and the end comes when a raider breaks through to the far row or when the last free raiders of one side are frozen or blocked and that side cannot finish a turn. Moving forward is the only thing a raider can do without capturing, so a game can never repeat itself and there are no draws.
